chunks: Al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man has a free woman under him; does he withdraw (coitus interruptus) from her?' He said, 'That is up to him; if he wishes, he withdraws, and if he does not wish, he does not withdraw.'

key_terms.إِلَيْهِ: It is up to him / his discretion
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: Free woman (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: Does the husband have the right to practice coitus interruptus with his free wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the husband holds unilateral discretion regarding 'azl' (coitus interruptus) with a free woman, reflecting the juristic view that it is a right of the male partner rather than a mutual obligation. This ruling underscores the flexibility in marital intimacy within Shia fiqh, distinguishing it from cases where the wife's consent might be more strictly required for other reasons. The emphasis on the husband's choice highlights the practical application of marital rights in early Islamic society.
